name: Ontario
summary: A British red ensign with the Ontario shield in the fly: three gold maple leaves on green under the red cross of St George. It was adopted in 1965, shortly after Canada replaced the Red Ensign with the Maple Leaf flag.
origin: When the national Maple Leaf flag replaced the Canadian Red Ensign in 1965, many in Ontario wanted to keep the British connection. Premier John Robarts's government adopted a red ensign with the provincial shield on 21 May 1965.

symbols.name: Three maple leaves
symbols.description: A sprig of three gold maple leaves on green.

symbols.name: St George's Cross
symbols.description: In the chief of the shield.
symbols.meaning: England and the province's British heritage.

facts: Its adoption was seen as a protest against the loss of the Red Ensign as Canada's flag.
Manitoba adopted a very similar red ensign the following year.
The shield was granted by Queen Victoria in 1868.
clues: A red ensign with a shield of three gold maple leaves under St George's Cross.
Adopted in 1965 to keep a link with a flag the country had just dropped.
A neighbouring province's flag is similar, with a bison.
